matrix.item: Onboard every investing entity as LVAI (≥₹10 Cr agreement)
matrix.rationale: Unlocks bespoke agreement, 100% unlisted headroom, CIV eligibility; a commercial relaxation only — it does not itself resolve the standing-instruction discretion question.

matrix.item: Legal-entity structuring proposal for the ₹500 Cr (individual/HUF/trust/holding co)
matrix.rationale: Every LVAI, AIF/SIF minimum, tax rate and FEMA route downstream depends on entity choice; currently unresolved across all seven design notes per compliance review.

matrix.item: AML/KYC/PMLA beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds framework
matrix.rationale: A ₹500 Cr single-mandate inflow triggers enhanced PMLA due diligence; absent from every design note reviewed — critical gap flagged by compliance critique.

matrix.item: Monthly omnibus Rebalance Proposal Pack (RPP) as sole consent instrument
matrix.rationale: Batches 50+ line items into one lawful, auditable client-directed instruction, satisfying Reg 24's per-trade direction requirement without per-trade friction.

matrix.item: Narrow, revocable Standing Instructions Register (sweeps, reinvestment, tranche execution, hedge roll)
matrix.rationale: Removes trivial friction on mechanical actions; downgraded from 'must' to 'should, pending legal opinion' per compliance critique until counsel/Informal Guidance clears it.

matrix.item: Pre-authorised sell-side de-risk trigger that self-executes without fresh consent (before legal clearance)
matrix.rationale: Regulatory and risk notes flag this unresolved; rebalancing/ops marked it 'must' in error. Route via same-day ad hoc mini-RPP until a legal opinion or SEBI Informal Guidance clears it.

matrix.item: Client-name segregated demat and bank accounts, no pooling
matrix.rationale: PMS Regulations require per-client custody; pooling this client's assets with any other client is a straightforward, easily-inspected breach.

matrix.item: Purpose-segregated demat accounts (Core/Tactical/Harvest) for FIFO management
matrix.rationale: FIFO is mandatory per demat account (Sec 45(2A)); segregation is the only lever for tax-aware lot selection and must exist before the first trade, not retrofitted later.

matrix.item: In-specie transfer-in of existing holdings at onboarding
matrix.rationale: Avoids a day-one tax event and preserves LTCG holding periods versus liquidating and re-buying into the NDPMS account.

matrix.item: Tax-aware rebalance hurdle rule (no STCG realisation unless alpha exceeds the tax gap)
matrix.rationale: Every 1% of AUM realised as STCG instead of LTCG costs ~1.8bps of NAV; this rule is the single largest controllable tax lever in the operating model.

matrix.item: Associate/group-security cap at 10% IPS (vs 15/25/30% SEBI ceiling), one-time consent + IC minute
matrix.rationale: Angel One is both group and executing broker; a tighter self-imposed cap plus real-time alert monitoring manages the structural conflict a captive wealth arm faces at inspection.

matrix.item: SEBI SCORES / Ombudsman grievance-redressal process and SLA
matrix.rationale: Standard registered-PM obligation, absent from every design note reviewed; needed in the Disclosure Document and client communication cadence.

matrix.item: Third-party PMS booked strictly outside NDPMS AUM, look-through reporting only
matrix.rationale: Reg 24 bars investing on another entity's advice; three critics independently flagged a draft that priced a PMS sleeve inside the ₹500 Cr book — corrected here to sit outside AUM.

matrix.item: Derivatives only as a pre-approved tail-hedge protocol, ≤25% notional, no leverage
matrix.rationale: Hedging/rebalancing is the only permitted derivative purpose under Reg 24; monthly RPP pre-approves notional and premium budget so hedge rolls need no fresh per-trade consent.

matrix.item: International sleeve via Indian-listed ETFs/FoFs only, ≤1% iNAV premium
matrix.rationale: Foreign securities are not yet permitted inside PMS; the USD 7bn MF overseas cap is near-exhausted, so buy-only-at-low-premium discipline avoids overpaying when creations are paused.

matrix.item: Adopt one canonical Model Master (16-line Moderate/Aggressive sleeve tables)
matrix.rationale: Four documents independently restated the SAA with different weights; one authoritative table (referenced, not re-derived) is required before any risk limit or cost budget is sized.

matrix.item: Core beta via Nifty 50/100 ETFs + index fund, AP/creation-unit route ≥₹25 Cr
matrix.rationale: 3-10bps TER, unlimited capacity, and AP dealing removes on-screen impact and price risk during the consent lag for the largest single sleeve (22-25% of AUM).

matrix.item: Factor tilt sleeve (Quality/Low-Vol/Momentum index funds), momentum capped 2-4%
matrix.rationale: Cheapest implementation of house style tilts; momentum's ~-60% historical drawdown and near-zero 1-yr return justify a hard cap, not a core weight.

matrix.item: Direct-equity NIFTY-750 scorecard book, 20-25 names, score×liquidity sizing
matrix.rationale: This is where the house's own quant alpha is owned; liquidity-capped sizing (≤20% of 5-day ADV, ≤3% NAV/name) keeps each consent-line trade executable within the monthly window.

matrix.item: Active MF sleeve restricted to mid/small-cap, direct plans, ≤1% of scheme AUM
matrix.rationale: Alpha persistence evidence exists in Indian mid/small, not large-cap; the 1% scheme-AUM ticket cap preserves exit liquidity and avoids becoming a capacity problem.

matrix.item: International equity 5% (Moderate)/7% (Aggressive) via India-listed ETFs/FoFs
matrix.rationale: Reconciled to the allocation model's own sleeve tables (not the 7.5% figure used elsewhere); park in arbitrage when AMC overseas-cap windows are paused.

matrix.item: Fixed income via target-maturity funds + direct G-sec/SDL, not debt mutual funds
matrix.rationale: Debt MFs are taxed as deemed short-term at slab (~39%) regardless of holding period; listed paper held >12m gets 12.5% LTCG — a permanent, avoidable tax drag otherwise.

matrix.item: Cap AA-rated corporate credit at ≤10% of the fixed-income sleeve
matrix.rationale: The original Moderate model's AA line (4% of AUM = 16.7% of the FI sleeve) breached the risk framework's own 90%-AAA/AA+ floor; trimmed here to close that inconsistency.

matrix.item: Gold 4-5% via ETF (AP route), silver capped at ≤1% of AUM
matrix.rationale: Gold's ~-0.10 correlation to Nifty is the cheapest tail offset; silver's ~27% volatility and -54% historical drawdown make it unsuitable beyond a tactical sliver.

matrix.item: Listed REIT/InvIT sleeve, 4-5 names, 2-4% of AUM
matrix.rationale: 6-10% distribution yield with partial tax-free return of capital and only ~0.35 correlation to Nifty 50.

matrix.item: AIF Cat II private credit, ~5% of AUM, 2 managers
matrix.rationale: NDPMS's 25% unlisted allowance is the mandate's structural edge over discretionary PMS; pass-through taxation and 11-15% net carry are largely uncorrelated to listed markets.

matrix.item: AIF Cat III / SIF hybrid long-short, 2.5-5% of AUM, prefer SIF where strategies overlap
matrix.rationale: SIF gets investor-level ~12.5% LTCG taxation versus Cat III's fund-level tax up to ~42.7% MMR on identical gross returns — a ~2pp post-tax edge on the same idea.

matrix.item: Deployment ladder: 8 weekly equity-like tranches (₹37.5 Cr) + 4 fixed-income tranches (₹30 Cr) + alternatives over 6-18 months, acceleration via pre-drafted mini-RPPs (Phase 1) / SI #7 (Phase 2)
matrix.rationale: Reduces cash-drag on a ~20x P/E, 8% still-below-peak market while keeping every acceleration step pre-authorised so a sell-off does not need a fresh mid-event consent.

matrix.item: Momentum factor allocation above 5% standalone (Moderate)
matrix.rationale: Semi-annual reconstitution turnover, ~-60% historical drawdowns at regime turns and a near-zero 1-year return make this a size-limited satellite, not a core holding.

matrix.item: Pooled/omnibus execution across clients or netting against Allocate books
matrix.rationale: PMS Regulations require client-name holding and a per-client instruction trail; aggregating orders in a house account is a straightforward custody/consent breach.

matrix.item: Hybrid band design (Strategy H): monthly review, trade breaches to inner band edge, plus event overlay
matrix.rationale: Simulation shows ~4.4% turnover and ~12bps p.a. cost+tax versus ~52bps for naive monthly-full rebalancing, while an event overlay still catches large excursions within 1-2 days.

matrix.item: Minimum RPP trade ticket ₹1 Cr (20 bps of AUM); every line ≥₹1.5 Cr except silver
matrix.rationale: Below this size transaction cost and consent overhead exceed the tracking-error benefit of trading; smaller drifts wait for the next monthly cycle.

matrix.item: Cash-flow-first rebalancing: inflows/dividends fund underweights before any overweight is sold
matrix.rationale: Closes drift at zero transaction cost and zero realised tax on a growing book; must be a pre-agreed standing instruction, not a per-month judgment call.

matrix.item: Route ETF legs ≥₹25 Cr via AP/AMC-direct; direct-equity legs ≥₹25 Cr via block-deal window
matrix.rationale: Saves ~10bps versus on-screen execution on a large ETF switch and avoids market impact on large single-stock tickets; requires an empanelled AP relationship before go-live.

matrix.item: Participation cap ≤10-15% of ADV/session; VWAP/TWAP staggering for tickets >2% of ADV
matrix.rationale: Controls market impact at ₹500 Cr scale without needing block-deal-sized tickets every month; keeps slippage within the 15bps-vs-arrival budget.

matrix.item: Annual LTCG-exemption harvesting and FY-end loss-netting review
matrix.rationale: Direct, low-risk tax alpha; LTCG losses can only offset LTCG gains, so netting must be planned client-wide before 31 March, not sleeve-by-sleeve.

matrix.item: Deployment-ladder acceleration as its own named Standing Instruction with a legal-opinion gate
matrix.rationale: A 12-week, ~50-line auto-accelerating deployment authorised by one week-0 signature is a stronger standing-discretion fact pattern than routine band trades; it was missing from the SI register entirely.

matrix.item: AIF capital-call funding as a pre-authorised standing sweep from the liquid/arbitrage sleeve
matrix.rationale: A missed ~10-business-day drawdown notice risks PPM default remedies (forced sale, forfeiture); this closes a real, avoidable money-losing gap the ops review identified.

matrix.item: Re-run the rebalancing Monte Carlo with common random numbers before relying on exact TE ranking
matrix.rationale: The current independent-random-path simulation shows tracking error falling as average drift rises across matched strategy pairs — a sign of simulation noise, not a real result.

matrix.item: Intraday trading, HFT overlays or options-overwriting inside the client account
matrix.rationale: Structurally incompatible with a per-instruction consent regime; if wanted, express it inside a Cat III AIF or SIF wrapper where the manager holds discretion.

matrix.item: 14-limit two-tier framework (sleeve/name/sector/AIF/manager/3P-PMS/credit/duration/illiquid/derivative/liquidity/FX/associate/absolute drawdown)
matrix.rationale: Two-tier house/legal limits with passive-vs-active breach handling give compliance and the IC one document to pre-clear every RPP against.

matrix.item: Parametric + historical VaR/CVaR and EWMA volatility (λ=0.94), daily
matrix.rationale: Parametric VaR alone understates fat-tailed Indian equity/credit risk (2018 IL&FS, 2020 COVID); the historical cross-check and same-day EWMA update catch regime shifts faster.

matrix.item: Tail-risk dashboard as a fifth tab on the existing IPS/attribution/deployment HTML suite
matrix.rationale: Shares the house palette and data pipeline rather than duplicating plumbing; NDPMS removes the option to react intraday, so the dashboard must surface breaches early enough for the 2-day consent SLA to still work.

matrix.item: 12-indicator early-warning board with USDINR anchored at the verified ~95.79 level
matrix.rationale: Corrects a stale ₹88/USD reference used in three design notes against the verified 11-Sep-2026 spot of ~95.79, which otherwise misjudges every FX-move threshold from day one.

matrix.item: Partial tail hedge: 95/85 put spreads on 25-40% of the equity sleeve, premium ≤1% AUM p.a., initiated when India VIX <15 (5% OTM put is the costing reference only)
matrix.rationale: At ~290bps p.a. (today's low VIX) the programme pays off strongly in sharp crashes but is a running cost in grinding regimes — partial, not full, notional coverage is the efficient size.

matrix.item: Cat III/SIF gross-notional (not NAV-only) look-through feeding the illiquid-aggregate limit
matrix.rationale: If Cat III leverage runs up to ~2x NAV, a nominal 4% AUM allocation could be ₹40 Cr of true gross exposure — materially changing concentration and VaR contribution versus a NAV-only view.

matrix.item: 2% always-on cash/arbitrage liquidity buffer
matrix.rationale: Funds the first days of any consent-latency gap in a crisis without touching the AIF or equity book.

matrix.item: Legal opinion / SEBI Informal Guidance on standing-instruction and de-risk-trigger design before go-live
matrix.rationale: The single biggest legal risk in the whole framework is recharacterisation as disguised discretion; better resolved before an inspection does it for the firm.

matrix.item: Tactical gold overweight (+2-3pp vs SAA) inside the existing rebalance band
matrix.rationale: No derivatives, no extra consent friction beyond the normal RPP line; gold rallied 30-38% in the GFC and tariff-shock windows.

matrix.item: Full-notional (100% AUM) unhedged derivative overlay
matrix.rationale: Running cost of ~290bps+ p.a. (~₹14.5 Cr/yr) on the whole book for a payoff that only shows up in sharp crashes and is a pure loss in the more common grinding regime.

matrix.item: Trigger-based automatic de-risking executed without a fresh per-instance client consent
matrix.rationale: This is disguised discretion under NDPMS and the single most likely finding in a SEBI inspection of the risk framework.

matrix.item: Daily TWRR engine, one fixed cash-flow convention, feeding the R0-R4 return hierarchy
matrix.rationale: A single engine prevents spreadsheet forks; separating paper, gross, net, and post-tax returns lets alpha, tax drag and implementation shortfall each be owned separately.

matrix.item: Client XIRR with IA min/median/max
matrix.rationale: Explicit SEBI/APMI requirement and the only fair lens on a staggered-deployment year where TWRR and XIRR diverge materially.

matrix.item: T1 APMI benchmark tagging (Multi Asset Strategy) with 7-working-day monthly filing
matrix.rationale: Non-negotiable regulatory floor; a benchmark change later requires an exit-load-free client exit offer, so getting T1 right at onboarding avoids a costly re-paper.

matrix.item: One canonical Policy Composite (T2) benchmark, single owner and sign-off date
matrix.rationale: Four documents produced four different 'policy composite' tables; alpha, fees and the IC scorecard all depend on one reconciled yardstick before the IPS is signed.

matrix.item: Brinson-Fachler attribution, Carino-linked, monthly, with look-through manager and factor splits
matrix.rationale: Separates TAA calls from manager/security selection when both are being judged; the worked-year example ties out exactly to the decimal and is worth keeping as the house standard.

matrix.item: Reconcile the PM fee to one rate (0.30% fixed) across every cost and alpha table
matrix.rationale: Regulatory/operations modelled 0.30% while performance modelled 0.50% for the identical fee line — a 20bp swing large enough to flip the net-alpha conclusion from roughly breakeven to clearly negative.

matrix.item: Disclose that Year 1-3 net alpha is expected near-breakeven to modestly negative pending fee/cost optimisation
matrix.rationale: On the allocation design's own CMAs, gross active return (+88bps) does not clear even the reconciled ~118bps of fees, opex, brokerage, implementation shortfall and realised tax — this must be disclosed, not hidden behind an unreconciled +100bps target.

matrix.item: Quarterly IC scorecard with named per-line owners, published to the client annually
matrix.rationale: Ties variable pay and client trust to specific, attributable line items (SAA, TAA, selection, implementation, costs, taxes) rather than one blended return number.

matrix.item: Do not present the house 80/20 benchmark as the mandate's headline target
matrix.rationale: The 7-sleeve Policy Composite is expected to trail the 80/20 by ~1-1.5% p.a. in strong equity years by design; conflating the two would misstate what the team is actually managing to.

matrix.item: Do not charge a performance fee on unrealised AIF marks
matrix.rationale: SEBI's fee circular ties performance fees to a high-water-mark principle on realised gains; unrealised AIF NAVs are themselves subject to stale-pricing risk.

matrix.item: Direct-with-AMC ETF dealing for any tranche ≥₹25 Cr
matrix.rationale: Cuts round-trip cost from ~15bps on-screen to ~5-7bps via the AP/AMC-direct route that exists specifically for this ticket size.

matrix.item: Rolling 3Y/5Y alpha-consistency screen for active MFs; direct-plan-only mandate
matrix.rationale: Point-in-time trailing returns overstate manager skill; rolling-window hit-rate is the closer proxy to persistence, and direct plans are a hard SEBI requirement, not a choice.

matrix.item: Fix the TCO tax-drag model before presenting a 'tax dominates cost' conclusion to the IC
matrix.rationale: The current model shows gold/silver/arbitrage/REIT annual tax drag exceeding those sleeves' entire expected return — a scaling bug independently caught by three reviewers; must be corrected before any client-facing TCO figure is used.

matrix.item: Discontinue new Sovereign Gold Bond purchases; use Gold ETF for all fresh gold exposure
matrix.rationale: SGBs have not been issued since Feb-2024 and Budget 2026 narrowed the capital-gains exemption to original subscribers held to maturity, removing the historic reason to buy in the secondary market.

matrix.item: Prefer SIF over Cat III AIF wherever the strategy overlaps
matrix.rationale: Investor-level ~12.5% LTCG taxation versus Cat III's fund-level tax up to ~42.7% MMR is a large, structural post-tax advantage on an identical gross-return idea.

matrix.item: No outsourcing of trade sizing, timing or execution to a third-party model or vendor
matrix.rationale: SEBI's May-2026 First Global order held that outsourcing 'investment decisions' this broadly — even via a technology vendor — is an absolute Reg 24(10) violation.

matrix.item: Onboard third-party PMS via APMI-vetted due diligence, structured as the client's own separate contract
matrix.rationale: Extends the addressable strategy set without building in-house capability; the same conflicts protocol used for Angel One group products must extend to any fee-paying referral relationship.

matrix.item: Consent ledger: every OMS order carries a foreign key to its RPP or standing-instruction ID
matrix.rationale: This is the actual inspection-proof of non-discretion, not a policy document; orders without a valid, unexpired match are blocked at release.

matrix.item: Aadhaar e-Sign/DSC consent capture with OTP-email fallback, both hash-logged
matrix.rationale: SEBI's digital-onboarding circular permits fully digital PMS consent artifacts; a hashed, time-stamped record is the primary evidence base at inspection.

matrix.item: IC of five voting members (CIO chair, PM, Head of Risk, Head of Compliance, independent advisor) plus non-voting Trading/Ops seat; quorum 4 of 5 incl. a non-investment vote
matrix.rationale: Corrects an internal miscount (Trading/Ops is explicitly non-voting); quorum should be stated as 4-of-5 voting members, not 4-of-6, to avoid an ambiguous governance bar.

matrix.item: Raise Ops/fund-accounting to 2.0-2.5 FTE and Compliance to a dedicated 1.0 FTE, with named backups
matrix.rationale: The original 1.5/0.5 FTE sizing leaves no rehearsed backup for the PM or Compliance sign-off seats; a single absence during a live event would stall the entire consent machinery.

matrix.item: Pre-trade compliance rule engine in the OMS (unlisted/associate headroom, no-leverage, MF direct-plan flag)
matrix.rationale: Automates the Reg 24 hard limits at order entry rather than relying on manual review across a multi-instrument book.

matrix.item: Extend the house cash-recon automation with an AIF capital-call ledger and bond/G-sec settlement leg
matrix.rationale: AIF units have no exchange order flow and the existing single-strategy recon assumes only listed instruments; without this extension the alternatives sleeve is invisible to daily monitoring.

matrix.item: Consent-tracker dashboard (RPP status, SLA breaches, standing-instruction log)
matrix.rationale: Turns the 2-day consent SLA from a policy statement into a monitored, escalating metric visible to Compliance and RM.

matrix.item: Redesign the client RPP as a one-page executive summary with full 50-line detail as an appendix
matrix.rationale: Walking a family through 50+ trade lines in 30 minutes every month either becomes a rubber-stamp or triples RM/PM time; track engagement depth as an operating KPI instead.

matrix.item: Dependency-gated build sequence: custodian → OMS rules → AP relationship, before parallelising automation
matrix.rationale: Custodian onboarding, OMS compliance-rule configuration and AP empanelment cannot realistically complete together in 30 days; sequencing avoids a rushed, unverified go-live.

matrix.item: Change-control/UAT gate for compute engines (risk model, TCO model, rebalancing simulation)
matrix.rationale: This project's own design phase produced a materially wrong tax-drag output that a basic peer review would have caught before it reached a client-facing conclusion.

matrix.item: Professional-indemnity insurance or a funded error-reserve backing the error-trade policy
matrix.rationale: The error-trade policy commits the firm to absorb certain losses via a segregated account, but no cost line currently funds that promise.

matrix.item: Second-mandate-ready platform build, not a bespoke one-off
matrix.rationale: Fixed operating cost (~₹1.8-3.2 Cr/yr) approaches the single mandate's fee revenue; the economics only work if a second NDPMS client can be onboarded on the same infrastructure within 12-18 months.

matrix.item: Client-signatory succession/incapacity annex (nominee, registered PoA, executor path, preservation mode)
matrix.rationale: Without it no one can lawfully approve an RPP if a sole individual signatory dies or is incapacitated; preservation mode keeps only mechanical SIs running.

matrix.item: Group-instrument best-execution control (group_instrument tag, second-broker/NAV routing, separate quarterly TCA bucket)
matrix.rationale: Angel One is both group and executing broker; inspection probes execution quality on group-product trades specifically.

matrix.item: Tax-adviser and index-licence/data-vendor engagement letters as dated gating deliverables
matrix.rationale: Load-bearing tax calls (TMF vs direct bond, REIT dividend, entity mix) and T2 index rights cannot stay 'review items' past day 15-20.

matrix.item: Realised drawdown-capture validation of the stress library (±10 pp tolerance per episode)
matrix.rationale: Capture ratios (39-63% / 62-81%) are single-pass model output until checked against realised NAV drawdowns.

matrix.item: FX-hedge decision costed (≈2.8% forward premium ≈ ₹0.7 Cr/yr on ₹25 Cr) and left unhedged by design
matrix.rationale: Currency risk is left open deliberately; the IC sees the bps cost of the choice, not just 'unavailable'.

matrix.item: Annual merge/IPS reconciliation with automated cross-check (reconciliation_checklist) and two-person sign-off
matrix.rationale: The stale-JSON/double-count error class caught in this review recurs at every FY-end IPS reset unless a named step exists.

matrix.item: Business-income-heavy Cat III tax scenario modelled alongside the SIF base case (rate grid 14.95% → 42.7%)
matrix.rationale: Cat III strategies vary widely on the capital-gains/business-income axis; the SIF edge ranges from +0.7 pp to +3.4 pp and reverses if the SIF is not equity-oriented.

matrix.item: NRI/FEMA branch (PIS/NRE/NRO accounts, repatriation basis, TDS u/s 195, DSC consent, time-zone SLA) if any family member is non-resident
matrix.rationale: One NRI holder changes custody, tax withholding, consent channel and the international-sleeve logic for that entity.

matrix.item: Higher-selection SAA (direct 12%, active 14%) quantified end-to-end as option (b) for the IC
matrix.rationale: Both SAAs the IC must choose between now carry a worked alpha, TE, cost and IR case.

matrix.item: Risk-tolerance questionnaire (10 questions, capacity vs willingness) and IC suitability minute
matrix.rationale: Suitability (why Moderate vs Aggressive for this family) is the first thing an inspection or dispute asks for.

matrix.item: Custodian contingency: ≥3 RFPs by day 5, decision by day 20, listed-only interim custody fallback, ladder start tied to custodian go-live
matrix.rationale: Custodian independence from the group is a hard requirement; a slow search must not pull the ladder forward on an unready stack.

matrix.item: Second-mandate pipeline with named owner and milestones (3 prospects/6m, term sheet/12m, signed/18m); break-even ≈₹1,000-1,400 Cr platform AUM at 0.30%
matrix.rationale: The platform's cost case rests on this happening; it needs an accountable owner.

matrix.item: Aggressive-variant TCO table reconciled (≈142 bps pre-PM-layer / ≈187 bps all-in)
matrix.rationale: If the client picks Aggressive the IC has a reconciled cost table; cost_bps in the data pack now ties to it.

matrix.item: PME (Kaplan-Schoar + Direct Alpha) for AIF sleeves, Campisi FI attribution and GIPS-style single-client composite — specified with formulas and worked examples
matrix.rationale: Named deliverables now have a spec, not just a label.
